recommendations.rationale: Distinguishing residual-motion/overshoot from slow settling requires a bounded numerical check (for example prediction_braking at a saved projected state or local_comparison), which is explicitly excluded from this initial read-only run.
No terminal/holding tip-speed weight or tuning change can be justified from raw weight magnitudes alone; defer until measured cost-term contributions and a full-trajectory view are available.

attribution.reason: Terminal position error is inside tolerance while terminal tip speed (0.635 m/s) stays roughly thirty times the 0.02 m/s limit and late-window speed peaks at 1.581 m/s; the configured terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight are 0.0. This is consistent with a still-moving tip near the goal, but raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance and no counterfactual replay is available to confirm it.

In the displayed final window the tip error falls monotonically (0.0581 to 0.00764 m) and speed declines after its peak, which is consistent with a trajectory that is still converging rather than one that has reached steady state; only the final window is displayed, so earlier behavior is not observed.

No full-trajectory record before t = 0.30 s is displayed and no error sign change or non-monotonic error is observable inside the shown window, so overshoot or a limit cycle can be neither confirmed nor excluded from retained evidence.

Every update is a deadline miss with mean update wall time about 17.08 s against a 0.01 s control period, and the effective horizon shrinks to 1 on the last update; however the task states wall deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so this cannot be claimed as the settling cause.

facts.statement: Across the retained final settling window the tip error decreases monotonically (about 0.0581, 0.0478, 0.0341, 0.0191, 0.0101, 0.00764 m at t = 0.30-0.35 s) while tip speed stays far above the configured 0.02 m/s settling limit, measuring 0.8619 m/s at t = 0.30 s, peaking at late_max_speed 1.581 m/s, and ending at terminal_speed 0.635 m/s.

Terminal reach passed (reach_passed = true; terminal_error_m = 0.00764 m < reach_tolerance_m = 0.01 m) while sampled_settling_passed = false against settling criteria position_limit_m = 0.01 m and speed_limit_m_s = 0.02 m/s, with late_max_error_m = 0.0581 m and late_max_speed_m_s = 1.581 m/s.

All 35 updates are flagged as deadline misses against a 0.01 s control period, with mean_update_s = 17.075 s; solver stopping counts are Solve_Succeeded = 1 and User_Requested_Stop = 34, and initialization_selected = 29 versus noninitialization_selected = 6.

Terminal and holding tip-speed cost weights are configured at 0.0 (terminal_tip_speed_weight, holding_tip_speed_weight) with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02 m/s and recipe horizon = 10, and the per-update effective horizon shrinks toward the end (3 at update 32, 2 at update 33, 1 at update 34).

gates.reason: Recorded terminal tip speed exceeds the configured settling speed limit.
Terminal tip error is within the reach tolerance, so reach passes while settling fails.

limitations: Single execution and a single controller/model configuration do not establish a dominant cause and do not prove input or causal-hypothesis equivalence.
The derived motion view displays only the final settling window (t = 0.30-0.35 s), so pre-window convergence behavior is not observed.
No historical optimizer iterations or full warm plans are reconstructed or retained.
Raw cost-weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions or scaling.
Wall deadline misses are documented not to inject physical delay into simulated time.
recommended_actions: Defer any numerical check (saved-state prediction evaluation, local_comparison, or prediction_braking) that could separate residual-motion/overshoot from slow settling, because numerical work is excluded from this run.
Defer any controller-parameter change until measured cost-term contributions and a full-trajectory view are available.
If authorized later, obtain the full-trajectory tip position/velocity records outside the displayed final window to test monotonic convergence versus overshoot.
